speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing significant symptoms, including fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, and weight loss. To help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if the abdominal pain is localized to a specific area?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the abdominal pain located in a specific area, such as the upper right or left quadrant? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, appetite, or skin color?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the swelling in your neck located above your collarbone, and have you experienced any fever or itching recently? I will also need to order a biopsy of that lymph node to determine the underlying cause. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy of cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index are highly suggestive of a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. To better characterize the disease and determine the stage, I need to see imaging of your chest, abdomen, and pelvis. REQUEST TEST: PET_CT_Scan

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Findings include massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms widespread lymphadenopathy involving the mediastinum, axilla, and neck, which aligns with the CD20-positive B-cell findings. Given the classic B-symptoms (fever/night sweats, weight loss) and lymph node involvement, I am confident in the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
